concepts.title: Pressure: Force per Unit Area
concepts.definition: Pressure measures how concentrated a force is: it equals the force acting perpendicular to a surface divided by the area over which it spreads, so a bag with broad straps feels lighter than a narrow one carrying the same weight.
concepts.key_idea: Same weight, larger area, smaller pressure - that is why broad straps comfort the shoulder.
concepts.textbook_ref: hecu106.txt lines 35-120 (pressure, bag straps, bucket handle)

solution_steps.explain: The perpendicular force spread over the surface gives the pressure.

concepts.title: Pressure Exerted by Air
concepts.definition: The atmosphere presses on everything from all sides because air has weight; atmospheric pressure is huge, yet we are not crushed since the pressure inside our bodies balances the pressure outside, as collapsing experiments with evacuated cans demonstrate.
concepts.key_idea: Air presses in every direction; internal balance hides its enormous size.
question_patterns: how do we know that air exerts pressure
why are we not crushed by atmospheric pressure
describe an activity to demonstrate air pressure
why does a flattened can crumple when air is pumped out
in which direction does air exert pressure
what keeps the atmosphere pressed to the earth

solution_steps.explain: Experiments with covered glasses and collapsing cans reveal air's pressure.
Fluids inside the body push outward, matching the atmosphere's inward push.
Air pressure acts equally in all directions.

concepts.title: Wind Formation by Pressure Difference
concepts.definition: Wind is moving air that always flows from a region of higher pressure toward a region of lower pressure; uneven heating of the earth creates these pressure differences, so sea breezes, land breezes and monsoon winds all begin as pressure contrasts.
concepts.key_idea: Air slides down the pressure gradient: high pressure to low pressure means wind.
question_patterns: how are winds formed
which way does air move between high and low pressure regions
why does a sea breeze blow during the day
how does uneven heating of the earth cause wind
explain the monsoon wind using pressure difference
what happens to wind speed when the pressure difference grows

solution_steps.explain: Uneven heating makes one region's air lighter and rising, lowering its pressure.
Cooler, heavier air from the high-pressure side rushes toward the low.
Sea breeze, land breeze and monsoon are daily and seasonal examples.

concepts.title: High-Speed Winds Lower Pressure
concepts.definition: Where air moves fast, its pressure drops - the rule behind flying balloons wobbling in a breeze and roofs lifting off in storms; slower surrounding air at higher pressure then pushes objects toward the fast stream.
concepts.key_idea: Blow over a paper strip and it rises: fast air means low pressure.
concepts.textbook_ref: hecu106.txt lines 468-519 (high-speed winds result in lowering of pressure)
question_patterns: what happens to pressure where wind speed is high
why do roofs blow off during storms

solution_steps.explain: Blow or fan air over the top of a light object.
The object moves toward the fast stream, showing reduced pressure there.
Storm winds racing over roofs lower the pressure above, and inside air lifts the roof off.

concepts.title: Storms, Thunderstorms and Lightning Safety
concepts.definition: Thunderstorms grow from strong upward winds in hot, humid conditions, building tall clouds where collisions create charges; lightning is the giant spark that discharges them, and safety lies in staying indoors, away from trees, poles and open fields.
concepts.key_idea: Charging clouds discharge as lightning - keep off open ground and tall objects.
question_patterns: how does a thunderstorm form
why does lightning occur during a thunderstorm
list the safety measures during lightning
why should one not stand under a tree during lightning
what is a lightning conductor and how does it work
how are thunderstorms and cyclones different

solution_steps.explain: Rising warm moist air builds towering clouds with strong up and down winds.
Charge separation inside the cloud discharges as a giant spark between cloud and ground.
Stay inside, avoid open fields, tall trees and metal; lightning rods guide strikes safely to earth.

concepts.title: Cyclones
concepts.definition: A cyclone is a huge, spinning storm born over warm seas: evaporating water releases enormous energy on condensation, low pressure at the centre sucks winds inward, and the earth's rotation spins the whole system, bringing destructive winds and storm surges to coasts.
concepts.key_idea: Warm ocean plus low pressure plus spin equals a cyclone; forecasts and shelters save lives.
question_patterns: how does a cyclone form over the sea
what is the eye of a cyclone
why do cyclones weaken after reaching land
what safety steps should coastal people take during a cyclone alert
how is a cyclone different from a thunderstorm
explain the role of water vapour in powering a cyclone

solution_steps.explain: Evaporation feeds moisture; condensation releases heat that powers the storm.
Air rushes to the low-pressure centre and spirals inwards due to the earth's rotation.
Forecasts, warnings, cyclone shelters and evacuation reduce the damage.
